newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Liberal candidate quits Vienna poll in race row.
newsitem.headline: Liberal candidate quits Vienna poll in race row.

text.p: The top Liberal party candidate in Vienna city elections quit in disgrace on Monday after it emerged he made racist remarks at a far-right political seminar in 1992.
Wolfgang Bachmayer announced his decision at a hastily-convened news conference with Heide Schmidt, leader of the Liberal Forum party, two weeks before the crucial October 13 vote.
"I have become too much of a political burden for the party," Bachmayer said.
The weekly news magazine Profil broke the news of Bachmayer's participation in the controversial 1992 seminar, organised by the nationalist Freedom Party, in its Monday edition.
According to Profil, Bachmayer had told the meeting that white babies began to cry when confronted with a black face.
Bachmayer initially defended his remarks as "scientifically correct", Profil said.
"Bachmayer's comments have made the Liberal Forum less convincing -- and not only in Vienna," Schmidt said.
He gave up his job as a market researcher with the Austrian OGM institute to switch to politics a few weeks ago.

The Liberal Forum, which was set up by Schmidt after defecting from the Freedom Party in February 1993, is putting up its first candidates in Vienna municipal elections, where Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats are battling to save their majority.
The Liberal Forum will name Bachmayer's replacement on Tuesday.
